title: Dedicated capacity weekly prep - 1:1 + weekly sync notes (Ryan Wood)
content:
Context / goal:
- Prep notes for weekly dedicated-capacity sync + 1:1 with Maria. Focus: next-quarter GPU pool forecast, reservation renewals, and autoscaling policy tuning.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Current dedicated GPU pool: 120 T4-equivalent slots (mix: 60 T4, 30 A10, 30 A100-d-edition equivalents after perf-normalization).
- Committed reservations: 90 slots reserved across three customers (monthly contracts). 30 slots unreserved/elastic.
- Short-term ask: decide on 20-slot burst reserve to cover upcoming marketing demo + expected ramp for two mid-market customers starting May.
- Risk: end-of-quarter cancellations could free up ~15 slots; need fast reallocation path.

Key metrics to cite in meeting:
- 7-day avg utilization: 72% overall; peak daily 88% (UTC peak window 14:00-17:00 PT).
- 30-day rolling avg latency SLO hits: 98.6% within 95th percentile target.
- Cost per token (hosted vs dedicated) - rough: dedicated saves ~28% at current batching levels.
- Cache hit rate (prefix KV): 18% overall; target to push to 30% for common internal prompts.

Forecast notes (next 90 days):
- Pipeline: 2 inbound customers (PoC -> Dedicated) expected conversion by late April; each needs ~8-12 A10 slots to start.
- Internal ramps: engineering sandbox usage increases ~10% after internal release next sprint (estimate +8 slots).
- Marketing demo week (first week of May): reserve 10 high-memory slots (A100-ish) for low-latency demos and fallback.
- Conservative capacity plan: add 25 slots to pool by April 20 (mix: 10 A10, 15 T4) to avoid saturation; hold 5 slots as immediate spare.

Reservations & contract renewals:
- Customer ACME Corp (contract ends 2026-05-15): currently 30 reserved slots. Renewal discussion scheduled w/CS on 2026-04-10. Need decision on offering a 12-mo discount vs month-to-month flexibility.
- Customer BrightApps: on trial reservation (10 slots) through 2026-03-31; engineering to monitor performance. If conversion expected, can commit additional 8 slots in May.

Autoscaling policy thoughts / proposals:
- Current policy: scale-up triggers at queue depth > 80% sustained for 4 minutes; scale-down cooldown 15m. Max burst = 30 slots.
- Proposal A (conservative): reduce scale-up sustain to 2 minutes for request spikes tied to demo/week windows; keep max burst 30. Improves latency but increases cost.
- Proposal B (cost-savvy): keep scale-up 4m but increase batching/queue headroom via aggressive prefix caching during expected demos to avoid unnecessary scale-ups.
- Proposal C (hybrid): temporary policy override capability per-customer (can allow higher burst for demo windows or paid burst add-on).
- Action: decide on default policy and documented override flow. Need SRE sign-off for safety.

Operational runbook gaps to highlight:
- Fast reallocation flow: need an automation (script/Runbook) to reassign freed slots to waiting customers within <10min. Currently manual and ~30-45min.
- Billing tie-in: when elastic slots used as burst, we must capture accurate usage to bill customers or attribute to marketing budget. Add tagging in runtime.

Open questions / discussion points for 1:1 with Maria:
- How aggressive should we be in pushing reservations vs keeping capacity elastic for flexibility? Maria prefers more reserved revenue; engineering prefers elasticity to avoid idle slots.
- Approve 25-slot incremental capacity purchase now (capex/commit) or wait until April 15 when BrightApps conversion more likely?
- Agreement on demo-week policy: do we offer free burst (marketing) or require internal chargeback?

Action items (owners + tentative dates):
- Ryan: draft PO/commit options for 25-slot add (options: 12-mo @ 10% discount vs monthly) - due 2026-03-09.
- Maria: confirm commercial playbook for demo burst (free vs chargeback) and communicate to marketing - due 2026-03-06.
- Liam: implement small runbook script to reassign freed slots (prototype) - due 2026-03-12.
- Jenna: add tagging for burst usage in telemetry pipeline + billing flag - due 2026-03-10.
- SRE lead (TBD): review autoscaling policy proposals and sign-off on override mechanics - request review by 2026-03-11.

Meeting agenda (30m sync):
- 0-5m: quick status and TL;DR numbers (util, reservations, peak risk).
- 5-15m: forecast review & commerce decision (25-slot ask and ACME renewal cadence).
- 15-22m: autoscaling policy proposals and runbook automation gap.
- 22-28m: assign action items and owners, confirm deadlines.
- 28-30m: any blockers / escalate to SRE or CS.

Notes to self (informal):
- Bring graph of utilization by region; most pressure is US-west (70% of peak).
- Prep quick cost delta slide: committed vs elastic at expected Q2 load.
- If ACME hints at churn, have option B (move 10 slots into reserved pool for new customers) ready.

Follow-ups after meeting (if approved):
- Submit capacity commit request to finance with 3 options (25 slots upfront, 12-mo discount, 6-mo mid option). Attach expected ROI calc.
- Kick off small runbook PR and schedule SRE review.
- Update internal capacity dashboard to flag demo-week windows and add reservation expiry alerts (7/3/1 day).

Quick reference links to paste in slides:
- Dedicated capacity runbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Dedicated+Capacity+Runbook
- Billing tagging spec (doc): https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/billing-tags
- Autoscaling policy RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812

Random notes / brainstorming (scratchpad):
- Consider offering a "demo buffer" for marketing as a paid add-on that guarantees 10 low-latency slots for a week. Price it as a small flat fee + token surcharge.
- Explore predictive scale-up based on scheduled demos / bookings (calendar-driven pre-warm). Could cut peak scale latency.
- Evaluate whether cache warming (scheduled KV pre-fill) could improve hit rate before demo windows.

End.
